title: Loom
description: An album cover woven from 96 threads each way, in twill, plain or satin, on a square cloth. Left alone it swishes from record to record on its own: the rows slide the next cover in from the right on a flowing wave, the columns slide it up from below in step, every thread overshoots a touch and settles, and each cover rests square for a beat before the next. Every thread carries the picture as an endless loop with a soft splice at the seam. Touch it at any point and it is yours: pull a row or column from the middle and hold it out and it keeps running forever while the shear wave drags the cloth after it; flick it and the whole cloth glides on and lands intact on a whole lap.
intent: One woven cover where pulling a single thread shears the whole cloth and plays it like a harp, with the next record weaving in row by row.

changelog.summary:
Every weft and warp thread now carries its cover as an endless strip: the shader wraps the sample coordinate per lap, so the picture loops instead of running out into the neighbouring record.
Lap seams are spliced, not cut: across a seam the strip blends into its mirror over about 4% of a width on an eased curve, and the splice fades out at rest so the cover stays crisp at the edges.
The thread spring is periodic: each thread rests in the nearest whole lap, so a pull past halfway lands on the next lap instead of springing back, and the old feel stays exactly the same inside half a width.
Neighbour coupling stays on raw positions, so pulling one thread from the middle drags its neighbours lap after lap and the shear wave spreads outward until the whole cloth flows.
Once everything slows down, the cloth gathers on its average lap and evens out, so it always comes to rest as the intact cover (no frozen kinks); positions are renormalised so the numbers never grow.
Pull drive: past 0.4 widths of pull the held thread keeps feeding at up to 7 widths a second for as long as you hold it out, so a pull from the centre in either direction runs forever while the cloth follows.
Keyboard: a tap of Shift with left or right still nudges the focused row; holding it now drives the row continuously until you release the key.
Plucks fire at every lap crossing, not only at home; a dragged thread ticks softly as each lap passes, fast threads pluck lighter, and flowing plucks are spaced at least 38ms apart.
Release flings go up to 14 widths a second (was 8), so a hard throw rolls over into the next lap.
The intro pulls the centre row two full laps to the right, the cloth flows after it, then everything settles back to the intact cover. This replaces the held S-curve.
Next and previous still weave the new record in row by row; rows that are mid-loop are wrapped to their nearest lap first, so the change always slides exactly one cover.
Fringe ends and the ply twist are now periodic in the offset, so nothing jumps when a thread completes a lap.
Hint, canvas label and page description now say that threads loop and the cloth follows.
Review fixes: a release now coasts. A flick hands its speed to every thread on a wide falloff (30% of the cloth either side, capped at 8 widths a second), so the whole cloth glides like a flywheel instead of snapping back to lap 0.
Gliding cloth aims for one shared lap, chosen at release from round(mean + mean speed / glide damping) and never behind the released row's own lap, so the cloth catches up to the thread rather than unwinding it.
While gliding the lap spring is softened by speed and the catch-up pull is capped at half a lap, then damping eases up to the landing value as it slows, so a throw lands within about a second with under a tenth of a lap of settle.
The cloth no longer gathers while its average is still moving faster than 0.15 widths a second, and a non-gliding gather homes on round(mean + mean speed / damping).
Releasing a held drive, the Shift-arrow key drive, or the end of the intro also glides, so a long pull lets go into a flowing finish instead of whipping back through its laps.
Drive is easier to reach and gentler: it starts at 0.18 widths of pull (was 0.4), gains 10 widths a second per width eased in over 0.1 widths, and tops out at 4 laps a second (was 7).
Flowing threads stay silent: a free thread passing into a new lap in the same direction no longer plucks; only reversals (oscillation and settling onto a lap) and crossings of its own lap pluck, so taps still strum exactly as before.
The held or driven thread ticks once per lap at 0.25 strength (was 0.4).
Pluck spacing applies only where it should: lap ticks of a held thread keep the 38ms gap, settling plucks on a new lap get 90ms, and ordinary tap and home strums are ungated again.
Pulls during a record change no longer drive while the weft is locked in transit, so they cannot wind rows against the absolute spring.
Grabs cannot get stuck: lost pointer capture cancels the grab, and a mouse move with no button down ends it.
Arrow auto-repeat no longer flips covers; an unshifted left or right while the key drive is running just releases the drive.
Hint and canvas label now mention that a flick glides on.

Idle loop: when nobody is touching it, the cloth swishes on its own through every cover in order, endlessly. Each swish slides the rows one full lap to the left on a flowing wave so the next record comes in from the right, then the cover rests square for 2.4 seconds before the next one.
The wave starts at one row and spreads outward with a rounded front, like a thread pulled from the cloth with the rest following. Each row eases in and out over 1.15 seconds and the far rows start up to 0.68 seconds later, so a swish takes about 1.8 seconds and peaks at about 1.4 widths a second. The lead row moves between swishes (centre, upper, lower, centre and so on) so the loop never repeats exactly.
Every swish lands every thread on exactly zero offset, so the cover always rests square and intact, with no leftover shear and no lap seams showing.
The columns follow the rows: each column turns over to the new cover with the existing pop as the average front of the rows passes it, from right to left. This replaces the fixed pop schedule only for swishes and for pulls made during one.
Swishes are silent. The plucks and lap ticks only sound once you touch the cloth.
Any touch takes over at once with no jump. Pressing, keys, next and previous stop the swish where it is, and the threads keep their position and speed and glide on from there. A light touch early in a swish settles back on the old cover; later it finishes on the new one.
While a swish is in flight each row is an endless strip with the old cover on one side and the new one on the other. Grab a row mid-swish and you have the full free cloth: hold it out and it loops forever, the cloth follows, a flick glides on. Pull to the right and the old cover comes back, pull to the left and the new one carries on. It always lands as one intact cover, and the caption and count follow whichever one it lands on.
Once the cloth lands, the strip turns back into the plain endless loop of one cover, so pulling it afterwards works exactly as before.
The idle loop eases back in 3 seconds after the last input (a press, a key, a nav click, a panel change, or the mouse moving over the cloth) and after the cloth has been still for 0.4 seconds. After the intro the first swish comes 1.8 seconds after the intro pull ends. When the cloth scrolls back into view it rests 1.4 seconds first.
Between swishes the frame loop stops completely and a single timer wakes it. Nothing runs while the tab is hidden or the cloth is offscreen; a swish caught by hiding is finished instantly out of sight.
No idle loop under reduced motion or with a single cover. With two covers it alternates.
The caption and count change with each swish through the same slide as next and previous, without calling back into the engine. Screen readers are not interrupted by the automatic changes; only manual changes are announced.
Square: the frame is pinned 1:1 and never flexes, and on phones it is now also bounded by the viewport height (at least 280px), so the square cloth fits with margin. The cloth origin snaps to whole device pixels for crisp edges. Covers are still centre-cropped to a square, so nothing stretches.
Hint, canvas label, page description and manifest description now mention that the cloth weaves through every record when left alone.

Columns now carry their cover as an endless strip with a lap window, exactly like rows, so a column changes record by sliding a full lap up (next) or down (previous) instead of popping in place. The pop is gone from every cover change; it is kept only for weave and thread count changes.
Idle swish: rows and columns are no longer scripted onto an eased curve. Each thread follows a moving anchor on that same 1.15 second curve through the cloth's own spring (tension, landing damping, neighbour coupling), so every thread lags a hair on the way out and lands with a gentle overshoot of about 3% of a width, then settles. The swish still lasts about 1.83 seconds and rests 2.4 seconds between records.
The column wave is centred on the row wave and runs right to left over 0.36 seconds, so rows and columns slide together as one sweep that brings the new cover in from the bottom right, instead of the columns trailing behind as a second wipe.
Next and previous: rows keep their staggered release and overshoot; columns are now held and released right to left (left to right for previous) from 170ms over 380ms and spring home with the same landing damping. Column landings stay silent so the strum sounds as before.
Rows and columns always land on the same record: whichever axis you last let go of decides the cover, and the other axis glides physically to the matching lap, a full lap if it has to, rather than switching. Interrupting a swish lets the rows decide and the columns follow; a slow release decides from where the cloth naturally comes to rest.
A chain only gathers onto its lap once it is within a quarter lap of it; further away it keeps gliding there, so a retargeted axis never snaps a whole lap on the stiff home spring.
Fringe ends no longer slide with the offset. The old ends followed sin of the offset, so they flipped direction halfway through every lap and the tail on one side vanished into the edge mid-swish; now the ends stay put and the thread runs through them.
Fringe colour now shows the strip continuing past the edge while a thread moves, so what leaves one edge is seen going out and what arrives is seen coming in from the other; at rest it shows the cloth's edge mirrored, so closing a lap window after landing never changes a pixel.
Next and previous after an interrupted pull wrap far-out threads back by whole laps before shifting instead of clamping them, so a thread wound far off no longer jumps by a fraction of a width.
Idle swishes stay silent, including the settle after the overshoot.
